Feluda.description: Prodosh C. Mitter, known as Feluda, is a private investigator and the central character of the stories, often addressed respectfully as Felu Babu.

Lalmohan Babu.description: Lalmohan Ganguli, popularly known as Lalmohan Babu or by his pen name Jatayu, is a writer of thrillers and a close friend and companion of Feluda.

Topshe.description: Feluda's cousin and the narrator of the stories who accompanies him on his investigations.

Three Musketeers.description: A reference to the famous trio from Alexandre Dumas's novel, used here to describe the team of Feluda, Topshe, and Jatayu.

Jaisalmer.description: A historic city in Rajasthan, India, known for its golden sandstone architecture; referenced as a place the characters visited.

Babu.description: A term of respect or endearment in Bengali and Hindi, often used after a person's name.

yoga.description: A physical, mental, and spiritual practice that originated in ancient India, commonly practiced for health and relaxation.

Nayan.description: A gifted boy with extraordinary numerical abilities whose real name is Nayan; he uses the stage name Jyotishka for Sunil Tarafdar's performances.

Chamakdar Tarafdar.description: The name of Mr Sunil Tarafdar's magic show, suggesting something dazzling or sparkling.

Mahajati Sadan.description: A prominent auditorium in Kolkata, often used for cultural events and performances.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car model, widely used in India especially in the late 20th century.

Nikunjabihari Lane.description: A street in Kolkata, indicating the local setting of the story.

Kalighat.description: A famous locality in Kolkata, known for the Kalighat Kali Temple and its cultural significance.

Bengali.description: Refers to the language and subject in which a character took an exam, also denoting the regional and cultural context.

paise.description: Paise is a subunit of the Indian rupee, where 100 paise equals 1 rupee; 'paisa' is the singular form.

Class X.description: Refers to the tenth grade in the Indian school system, an important academic year.

Sunil Tarafdar.description: A young, ambitious magician and showman whose performances are central to the story; he is the employer of Nayan.

Srinath.description: The cook in Feluda's household, who serves tea to the guests.

Mr Reddy.description: A theatre owner from Madras who invites Mr Tarafdar to perform there.

Sam Kellerman.description: An American impresario interested in showcasing Nayan's abilities in America.

Ekdalia Road.description: A street in Calcutta (Kolkata), where Mr Tarafdar's house is located.

Badshah.description: The name of Mr Tarafdar's Alsatian dog, known for being a good watchdog.

Madras.description: The former name of Chennai, a major city in South India.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India.

City Bank of New York.description: A major American bank, referenced in relation to Mr Kellerman's account.

Miracles Unlimited.description: The name of the company to be formed by Mr Tarafdar's sponsor for his magic shows.

samosa.description: A popular Indian snack consisting of a fried or baked pastry with a savory filling, such as spiced potatoes, peas, or meat.

bearer.description: A servant or attendant, especially in Indian households, responsible for serving guests and carrying items.

T H Syndicate.description: A business entity involved in imports and exports, with an office on Pollock Street.

Pollock Street.description: A street, presumably in Calcutta, where T H Syndicate's office is located.

metro rail.description: A rapid transit system, likely referring to the urban railway in Calcutta.

Tarak Nath Thakur.description: A wealthy and eccentric collector of unusual people and animals, often referred to as Mr Thakur or by the initials TNT.

Kichomo.description: A Korean dwarf, described as the smallest adult in the world, and part of Mr Thakur's collection.

Tokobahani.description: A Maori secretary in Mr Thakur's collection, notable for being able to write with both hands simultaneously.

Gawangi.description: A man from Uganda, nearly eight feet tall and extremely strong, who is Mr Thakur's personal companion.

Maori.description: An indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, referenced here as the ethnicity of Mr Thakur's secretary.

Laxmanjhoola.description: A place in India, likely referring to Laxman Jhula, a famous suspension bridge and pilgrimage site in Rishikesh.

Uganda.description: A country in East Africa, the homeland of Gawangi.

Kampala.description: The capital city of Uganda, mentioned as Gawangi's hometown.

Terai.description: A region of lowland plains at the base of the Himalayas, known for its jungles and wildlife.

Olympic.description: Refers to the Olympic Games, an international sporting event, used here to compare Gawangi's strength.

New York Times.description: A prominent American newspaper, mentioned as having published an article about Mr Thakur.

Vedas.description: The four ancient sacred texts of Hinduism, referenced in a discussion about the number four.

sadhu.description: A Hindu holy man or ascetic, often known for spiritual practices and renunciation.

Nayan’s father.description: Ashim Sarkar, a poor man working in a post office, father of Nayan.

Shankar Hublikar.description: Tarafdar's efficient manager and friend, originally from Maharashtra but raised in Calcutta.

Bhagirath.description: The chowkidar (watchman) at Tarafdar's house, who encounters the 'giant' intruder.

Maharashtra.description: A state in western India, referenced as Shankar Hublikar's origin.

Coromandel Express.description: A well-known express train running along the eastern coast of India.

Taj Coromandel.description: A luxury hotel in Madras (now Chennai), where the characters plan to stay.

shawl-walla.description: A street vendor or seller of shawls, often from Kashmir.

paanwalla.description: A person who sells paan, a preparation of betel leaf chewed in South Asia.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'hello' or 'greetings'.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or security guard, especially for residential or business premises.

goraila.description: A Bengali/Hindi pronunciation of 'gorilla', used here to describe a large, ape-like creature.

Alipore Park Road.description: A locality in Kolkata, India, known for its upscale residential area.

Contessa.description: An Indian-made car model, popular in the 1980s and 1990s.

St Xavier’s College.description: A prestigious educational institution in Kolkata, India.

Belle Vue clinic.description: A well-known private hospital in Kolkata.

goondas.description: A Hindi term for hired thugs or hooligans.

South India.description: A geographical region of India, indicating Feluda's travel destination.

Hotel Coromandel.description: A hotel in Madras (Chennai), where Feluda and others plan to stay.

sahib.description: An honorific term from Hindi/Urdu, used to address men respectfully, especially in formal or colonial contexts.

Basak.description: An antagonist implicated in threatening Nayan and suspected of involvement in criminal activities.

New Market.description: New Market is a famous shopping area in Kolkata, known for its variety of stores and eateries.

Ideal Stores.description: Ideal Stores is a shop located in New Market, mentioned as the source of a cash memo.

Hullabaloo in Honolulu.description: Hullabaloo in Honolulu is a book title written by Jatayu, used humorously in the conversation.

Shabash.description: A Hindi word meaning 'well done' or 'bravo,' used to praise someone.

Henry Hodgson.description: A Christian gentleman with a passion for horse racing who poses as a reporter to seek Nayan's help with winning bets.

Whitaker.description: An American who created the snake park in Madras, mentioned as a notable figure.

Mr Hingorani.description: A client of Feluda and partner in the T H Syndicate who acts as the secret sponsor of Tarafdar’s show.

Mohan.description: Mr Hingorani’s nephew, who informed him about Jyotishka.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, referenced as a major metropolis.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major city on the west coast of India.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, known for its vibrant culture and history.

Elephanta.description: Refers to the Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site near Mumbai.

Ellora.description: A site in Maharashtra, India, famous for its ancient rock-cut caves and temples.

Orissa.description: The former name of Odisha, a state in eastern India known for its temples.

Mahabalipuram.description: A historic town in Tamil Nadu, India, known for its ancient temples and rock-cut monuments.

Rohini Theatre.description: A theater in Madras where Mr Tarafdar is scheduled to perform his show.

the Hindu.description: A major English-language newspaper published in India.

Faizabad.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, mentioned as the location of Mr Hingorani’s ancestral home.

p.m..description: Post meridiem, Latin for 'after midday', commonly used in India to denote time after noon.

The Crocodile’s Crunch.description: A book written by Lalmohan Babu (Jatayu), mentioned as a gift for Nayan.

The Astounding Atlantic.description: Another adventure book authored by Jatayu, referenced in the chapter.

shore temple.description: A famous ancient temple in Mahabalipuram, known for its scenic seaside location and Pallava architecture.

Gangavataran.description: A monumental rock relief in Mahabalipuram depicting the descent of the Ganges river from the Himalayas.

Mahishasurmardini Mandap.description: A rock-cut cave temple in Mahabalipuram dedicated to the goddess Durga slaying the demon Mahishasura.

Pancha Pandava caves.description: A group of rock-cut caves in Mahabalipuram, named after the five Pandava brothers from the Mahabharata.

Pallavas.description: The Pallavas were an ancient South Indian dynasty responsible for building many monuments in Mahabalipuram; 'Ballabhas' is a mistaken reference to them.

Pandava.description: Refers to the five heroic brothers from the Indian epic Mahabharata, after whom several monuments in Mahabalipuram are named.

Draupadi.description: The wife of the five Pandava brothers in the Mahabharata, with a chariot-shaped monument named after her in Mahabalipuram.

Ganges.description: A sacred river in India, whose mythological descent to earth is depicted in the Gangavataran relief.

Himalayas.description: The mountain range in northern India, from which the Ganges is said to descend in Hindu mythology.

Detecnique.description: A rival detective agency and its associated enigmatic figure suspected of criminal involvement.

Mysore.description: The name of the hotel dining room, likely referencing the city of Mysore in Karnataka, India.

Moghlai.description: A style of cuisine originating from the Mughal Empire, known for its rich and aromatic dishes.

Mahishasur.description: A demon from Hindu mythology, often depicted in temple sculptures.

Ghatotkach.description: A character from the Mahabharata, the son of Bhima, known for his immense size and strength.

Mahabharata.description: The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic, referenced in the story as both a play and a movie, featuring many legendary characters and stories.

ayurveda.description: A traditional Indian system of medicine based on natural remedies and holistic practices.

Sarpagandha.description: A medicinal herb used in ayurveda, known for its use in treating high blood pressure.

Indian Airlines.description: A former major domestic airline in India, now merged with Air India.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, known for its casinos and as a travel destination.

mandaps.description: Mandaps are pillared halls or pavilions in Indian temples, often used for religious rituals; 'mandap' is the singular form.

bell-boy.description: A hotel staff member responsible for carrying guests' luggage and assisting with other tasks.

couped up.description: A variant spelling of 'cooped up', meaning confined in a small space, often used in Indian English.

Devkinandan Tiwari.description: A man involved in a theft case and a client seeking help to remember the combination to his chest; he is part of the T H Syndicate.

Jyotishkam.description: A term possibly referring to someone involved in astrology or a specific person needed for the show.

lakhs.description: A unit in the Indian numbering system equal to one hundred thousand (100,000); 'lakh' is the singular and 'lakhs' is the plural form.

instalment.description: A partial payment of a sum of money due, commonly used in Indian financial transactions.

auspicious.description: Considered to bring good fortune or luck, often used in Indian cultural and religious contexts.

Miss Swaminathan.description: The lady in charge of the hotel bookshop, who provides key information about the book purchases.

Inspector Ramachandran.description: The police inspector who arrives to take charge of the suspects.

The Manchurian Menace.description: The title of Lalmohan Babu's next book, referencing Manchuria, a historical region in Northeast Asia.

China.description: A country in East Asia, referenced in relation to Lalmohan Babu's book research.

Mandarins.description: Refers to high-ranking officials in imperial China, mentioned as the setting for Lalmohan Babu's story.
